text:
Mei Tan: Hey team  first day! Trying to boot the local compose stack (web + postgres + redis) on my MacBook (M1). Postgres container starts but my local app (run on host) can't connect. I tried localhost:5432 and host.docker.internal:5432, both fail. Also noticed an error in the PG container about failing to write to /var/lib/postgresql/data. Any recommended dev-friendly workflow?

Oliver Brooks: Welcome Mei! Two quick things: (1) if your app is running on the host, use host.docker.internal, not a unix socket. The container's unix socket isn't shared with your host. (2) The write error is usually a mount permission problem when using a host bind-mount. Are you bind-mounting ./pgdata to /var/lib/postgresql/data?

Mei Tan: Yes I have: - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data in compose. Docker logs show permission denied when postgres tries to create PG_VERSION.

Rashmi Singh: On macOS that happens because the container runs as user 999 and the host dir is owned by your user. Quick workaround: sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata then docker-compose up -d postgres. Better: switch to a named volume so Docker manages permissions: 
```yaml
volumes:
  pgdata:
services:
  postgres:
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```
We usually prefer named volumes for local dev on mac.

Mei Tan: OK switching to named volume fixed the write error, thanks. But host.docker.internal:5432 still times out. I verified compose has ports: - "5432:5432". Any other conflicts?

Oliver Brooks: Check for a host postgres running (homebrew). `brew services list` and stop it if needed. Also if you previously mapped the same port and the host had something bound, compose might have failed to publish. An alternative is to map host port to a high port like 15432:5432 and connect to host.docker.internal:15432.

Rashmi Singh: Another gotcha: PGDATA env mismatch. If your compose sets PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata but you mount to /var/lib/postgresql/data directly, postgres may treat the dir as non-empty and skip init. Confirm your compose and any ENTRYPOINT expectations match.

Mei Tan: Hmm my compose sets PGDATA to /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata and I mounted the volume to /var/lib/postgresql/data. That could be it. What happens if initialization is skipped? My init SQL in ./db/init isn't executed.

Oliver Brooks: The official entrypoint runs init scripts only when it detects an empty data dir at PGDATA path. If the paths don't line up, postgres thinks data exists and skips initialization. To fix: make the volume mount match PGDATA or unset PGDATA so default is used, then recreate volumes: `docker-compose down -v` and remove the named volume with `docker volume rm <name>` or `docker volume prune` (dev caution: deletes data). After recreate the init scripts will run.

Mei Tan: Great, I'll align the mount with PGDATA and nuke the volume. Last question: is it normal to run the dev web server on host or run it in the compose service? Which is less friction?

Rashmi Singh: Both are common. Running the web service in compose avoids host<->container networking issues (use service name postgres) and is reproducible. Running on host is fine too but requires ports and host.docker.internal. We keep an opt-in docker-compose.override.yml for dev that adds the web service for folks who want full-in-docker.

infra-helper-bot: FYI: dev guide with recommended compose snippets, .env.local.template, and Mac M1 tips: https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-setup. Use port range 15xxx for mapped host ports to avoid conflicts.

Mei Tan: Thanks everyone  that gives me a clear checklist. I'll fix PGDATA/mount, recreate the volume, and try web-in-compose if host still misbehaves. Will ping if stuck.
